skill.name: project-scaffolding
skill.description: Project scaffolding wizard for creating web, mobile, backend, desktop, extension, and monorepo applications with guided framework choices, configuration templates, and starter project files.
skill.summary: Create configured starter projects across many frameworks with guided setup and reusable templates.
skill.author: hmohamed01

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by documentation, framework examples, generated code fences, and placeholder environment templates. Confirmed risks are limited to intended scaffolding behavior: external CLI use, public CDN use in generated HTML, container binding to all interfaces, default development credentials, and predictable generated secret-key fallbacks.

remediation.issue: External scaffolding commands can run package-manager or framework CLI code.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running native CLIs, package managers, or the Python scaffold script, and show the exact command first.

remediation.issue: Generated Django templates include predictable SECRET_KEY fallback values.
remediation.suggestion: Generate a random development secret per project or fail startup when SECRET_KEY is missing outside local development.

remediation.issue: Generated compose examples include default database credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Mark credentials as local-only placeholders and encourage users to replace them before sharing or deployment.

remediation.issue: Some generated templates use public CDN assets or bind services to all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Offer local asset installation options and document when 0.0.0.0 should be changed to localhost.

content.value_statement: Starting a new project requires many framework and configuration choices. This skill guides setup and creates practical starter files for common application types.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through project type, framework, language, styling, database, and tooling choices.
Supports many starter types, including web apps, APIs, mobile apps, desktop apps, extensions, and monorepos.
Can generate project structures, configuration files, example source files, README files, and environment templates.
Provides reference material for framework-specific structures and best practices.
Can use a Python scaffolding script or native framework CLIs when the user approves execution.
limitations: Generated projects still need dependency installation and local testing by the user.
Some templates include development-only placeholders that must be changed before deployment.
Native CLI flows depend on the user environment and installed toolchains.
The skill creates starter code and does not replace architecture review for production systems.

use_cases.title: Create a web application starter
use_cases.description: Generate a React, Next.js, Vue, Astro, Remix, or SvelteKit project with selected styling and tooling.

use_cases.title: Start a backend service
use_cases.description: Create an API scaffold with framework choices, database configuration, environment templates, and basic project structure.

use_cases.title: Prototype cross-platform apps
use_cases.description: Set up mobile, desktop, extension, or monorepo starter projects with guided configuration choices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple starter
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new React project for a small dashboard. Use TypeScript, simple styling, and a clear folder structure.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a framework interactively
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a framework for a content-heavy marketing site, then scaffold the project after I confirm the choices.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a backend with database setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Create an API starter with configuration files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scaffold a FastAPI service with PostgreSQL, environment templates, migrations, tests, and development instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a full starter workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a monorepo with a Next.js web app, a backend API, shared TypeScript packages, linting, tests, and Docker development setup.

output_examples.input: Create a Next.js app with TypeScript, Tailwind, Prisma, and PostgreSQL.
output: A guided list of selected options.
A generated project structure with app, database, and configuration files.
Setup notes for installing dependencies and updating environment placeholders.

output_examples.input: Scaffold a Django API for a small internal tool.
output: A backend starter with settings, app structure, database configuration, and README guidance.
Warnings about replacing development secrets before deployment.

output_examples.input: Create a static landing page starter.
output_examples.output: A simple website scaffold with assets, styling configuration, development commands, and deployment notes.

best_practices: Review all generated environment files and replace placeholders before deployment.
Confirm external CLI commands before running them, especially package-manager commands.
Run the generated project locally and execute its tests before adding production features.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy generated projects with default secrets or database credentials.
Do not run native scaffolding commands without checking the exact command and target directory.
Do not treat scaffolded code as production-ready without security and architecture review.

faq.question: What kinds of projects can this skill create?
faq.answer: It supports many web, backend, mobile, desktop, extension, serverless, and monorepo starters.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It may recommend scaffold scripts or native CLI commands, but users should approve command execution first.

faq.question: Can I customize framework choices?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed to ask for project type, framework, language, styling, database, and tooling preferences.

faq.question: Are generated projects production-ready?
faq.answer: No. They are starter projects and need dependency review, secret replacement, testing, and deployment hardening.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I review after generation?
faq.answer: Review generated commands, package dependencies, environment templates, default credentials, and network-facing settings.
